note: Four of five, failing on the one criterion this corpus keeps failing on. 'successful' is met — he runs his own contracting business, confirmed at 00:39:43. 'good_to_great' is met almost definitionally; the entire call is framed around a plateau he wants to break, 'I just feel like I'm capable of being at that next level of shape that I just can't seem to get over.' 'not_deconditioned' is emphatic: 30 miles a week, 1,500 miles in the past year, a 40 lb loss already banked, and he lifts twice a week. 'neglected_health' is met in the sense the criterion intends — health is not in crisis and is being actively managed, and the neglected years are behind him. 'income' is the miss and it is verified rather than inferred: he confirmed 'I don't have the full amount right now', declined to state cash on hand or account balances, and volunteered 'money's tight, man' with three children at home. He is not poor — he owns a business and would proceed instantly if the cash were there — but he fails the affordability test as the ICP writes it. That makes three of the four sales calls in this batch so far blocked on liquidity rather than on belief, alongside Marian Samson and Fletcher Koder, and it is a direct echo of the standing observation in the ICP file that 'makes good money' is doing work a payment plan already solves. Billy Collazo is the strongest case for that argument in this batch: fully committed, textbook ICP on every other axis, and stopped only by not having $6,000 in one piece on a Saturday.
